blocks.heading: Reply.io cost scenarios to pressure-test
blocks.body: Price Reply.io against how you actually buy seats and unlocks — not against a competitor's homepage headline.

scenarios.title: Lean team / free-or-trial first
scenarios.body: Scope a time-boxed pilot; No free/trial flag confirmed in SG data — budget a paid pilot.

scenarios.title: Growing team with gated workflows
scenarios.body: Map must-have workflows (contact management, email sequences, lead scoring) to plan unlocks before expanding seats.

scenarios.title: Hidden / extra cost watch
scenarios.body: Budget risk: Reply Data is a bundled convenience layer rather than a specialist database with published coverage figures. Also check add-ons, overages, and admin time outside the sticker plan.

items.title: Cost trap 1
items.body: Reply Data is a bundled convenience layer rather than a specialist database with published coverage figures

items.title: Cost trap 2
items.body: Jason AI SDR and Agency tiers are quote-gated, so the top of the plan ladder is not self-serve

items.title: Cost trap 3
items.body: Mailbox warmup, LinkedIn accounts, and data credits create ongoing operational overhead per seat

items.title: Cost trap 4
items.body: LinkedIn automation carries platform compliance risk some organizations cannot accept

items.title: Cost trap 5
items.body: No free plan — evaluation runs through a time-limited trial only

blocks.title: Cheaper or clearer alternatives to pressure-test
blocks.body: Compare total cost of ownership vs Reply.io on identical constraints.
